newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME ALUMINIUM SEEN SLIGHTLY UP, ZINC TO SINGAPORE.
newsitem.headline: LME ALUMINIUM SEEN SLIGHTLY UP, ZINC TO SINGAPORE.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) aluminium prices are seen posting further gains later on Tuesday while reports circulated in the trade that 20,000 tonnes of zinc will be arriving in warehouses here shortly, dealers said.
"Aluminium still has some upside to it," a dealer said.
Another trader said aluminium, although overbought, was still attracting "some buying in the market".
"I think aluminium will still pick up a little bit, maybe by US$10-$15 (a tonne)," one dealer said.

Brokers Rudolf Wolff said in its daily review that aluminium's positive close might indicate "renewed challenges on overhead resistance, though we still feel that further consolidation is required before aluminium can successfuly sustain new highs".
Three-month aluminium was seen by one metal house at 0230 GMT at $1,749/52 a tonne, down slightly from the late indication on the LME of $1,750/52 a tonne.
Zinc prices are tipped to be steady to slightly higher with reports going around the market that more Chinese zinc is due to arrive in warehouses in the city-state.
"Most likely, zinc will just be in a range," a dealer said.
"People are still squeezing the market. They believe there are shorts and the Chinese have not fully covered their positions," another trader said.
Brokers Brandeis said in a daily report that zinc's "primary uptrend is still intact and thus capable of fuelling more gains in due course".

Traders said up to 20,000 tonnes of zinc from China would be placed in warehouses here. The volume of zinc in the LME's Singapore warehouse has ballooned to 50,325 tonnes on Monday, up from 12,800 tonnes reported at the end of April.
Three-month zinc was seen by a metal trading company at 0230 GMT at $1,543/48 a tonne against the kerb close of $1,545.
Copper prices were seen doing very little with consumption soft due to the summer holiday season.
"I don't feel good about copper. It's looking bearish because there's not much consumption during the summer," a dealer said.
Copper prices were seen by the trade at 0230 GMT at around $2,284/89 a tonne against the late indication on the LME of $2,282/87.
